introduction.text: Piazza Navona is a public open space in Rome, Italy, built on the site of the 1st century AD Stadium of Domitian. It retains the stadium's elongated oval form and became a significant showcase for Baroque design in the 17th century.

history.description: The site of Piazza Navona was originally the Stadium of Domitian, constructed by Emperor Titus Flavius Domitianus.
The area was defined as a public space in the last years of the 15th century when the city market was moved there from the Campidoglio.
Piazza Navona was transformed into a significant example of Baroque Roman architecture and art during the pontificate of Innocent X.
From 1652 until 1866, the piazza was intentionally flooded on Saturdays and Sundays in August for elaborate celebrations by the Pamphili family.
The pavement level of the piazza was raised during the 19th century.
The market was moved from Piazza Navona to the nearby Campo de' Fiori in 1869.
In 2011, the Fontana del Moro was damaged by a vandal who decapitated some of its figures.
After the Fall of the Western Roman Empire, the stadium fell into ruin and its materials were quarried for other buildings.
A Christmas market is held annually in the piazza from early December to early January.

design.description: Piazza Navona retains the elongated oval form of the 1st century AD Stadium of Domitian, on which it was built.
The piazza became a significant showcase for Baroque design in the 17th century, featuring works by prominent architects and sculptors.
The central Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi, completed in 1651, was designed by Gian Lorenzo Bernini and features an obelisk.
The Church of Sant'Agnese in Agone was designed by Francesco Borromini, Girolamo Rainaldi, and Carlo Rainaldi.
The Palazzo Pamphili, facing the piazza, was designed by Girolamo Rainaldi and includes a long gallery by Francesco Borromini.
At the southern end, the Fontana del Moro features a basin and four Tritons sculpted by Giacomo della Porta in 1575.
The Fountain of Neptune at the northern end was also created by Giacomo della Porta in 1574.

art.description: Gian Lorenzo Bernini sculpted the Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi, completed in 1651, which is topped by the Obelisk of Domitian.
The long gallery within the Palazzo Pamphili features frescoes by Pietro da Cortona.
In 1673, Gian Lorenzo Bernini added a statue of a Moor wrestling with a dolphin to Giacomo della Porta's Fontana del Moro.
Antonio Della Bitta added the statue of Neptune to Giacomo della Porta's Fountain of Neptune in 1878 to balance the Fontana del Moro.
